raw_text: Linux mounts USB drives by filesystem label rather than by port or controller enumeration order, which is how Windows assigns drive letters. This property is architecturally important for a two-drive rotation scheme: either drive can be plugged into any USB port and will mount under its own label, allowing a script to detect it by name without any configuration change. The Windows approach of enumerating by hardware competition means the same drive can receive a different letter depending on which port it uses, making label-independent detection fragile. Label-based mounting is the enabling condition for a portable, plug-any-drive backup script.
